body.intent: Workflow dispatch: every run the daemon starts goes through repo-defined selection rules (in rhiza.toml) that map a trigger (request queued, change set accepted and ready) and the request's kind (feature, bug, milestone) to a workflow, and rhiza request --workflow <name> overrides the choice for one request; the change set records the kind and any workflow its request chose so the ship pick follows it. Today daemonStartPlan always starts planWorkflow 'plan' (internal/api/run.go:763) and a ready change set always gets defaultWorkflow 'ship-change' (run.go:1257); workflow-overrides only shadow those names. Built-in default rules reproduce today's behaviour, so a repo adds e.g. a bugfix workflow in .rhiza/workflows/ and maps bug to it without changing Rhiza. Relates to the workflow-authoring change set 01M6HN24. Follows decision workflows-are-the-rules (PR #353): every rule is workflow policy the owner defines, Rhiza ships defaults and enforces only references between nodes.
